clue.text: Travel-a way to get to eg Japan

definitions.note: the clue names one country standing for the whole region it belongs to

parts.note: to fare is an old verb for to travel or journey
ST, short for street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone asks which route will take them to Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg Japan' is a loose definition by example: Japan is one of the countries of the region, so it stands for the region as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan lies in the easternmost part of Asia, the region Europeans traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Mad 'to raise it In foreign money

indicators.note: In means the raised word goes inside the currency

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France, Belgium and Switzerland

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A frenzied attempt to raise funds in a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to raise' reads a word upward, so it turns; the franc was the money of France and Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wildly agitated, distraught, as if mad with worry.

clue.text: Will proof follow, concerning this ne'er-do-well ?

indicators.note: follow means the will proof comes after the word for concerning

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
probate is the legal proving of a will

explanation.surface: A legal question about whether proof of a will follows for some scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Probate is the court process that proves a will is valid; 'follow' places it after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a scoundrel or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Adamson met East by the poplar

parts.note: read as Adam's son: Abel was a son of Adam in Genesis
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A man called Adamson met someone from the East beside a poplar tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Adamson', which looks like a surname but splits as Adam's son.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Occasion on board familiar : to passenger

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an occasion is a time, as in 'the first time'
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Some occasion on board ship is familiar to a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a schedule of departures is the thing every passenger knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A published schedule of departures and arrivals is what a regular traveller consults and knows well.

clue.text: This time Tommy's getting nowhere

parts.note: a Tommy is a British soldier; on the parade ground he can lift his feet in step without moving forward, and the answer put before 'time' names that drill

explanation.surface: A British soldier finds he is making no progress this time.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier. The answer followed by the clue's 'time' gives the drill phrase for stepping on the spot, which also means making no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill of stepping in place without advancing gives the idiom for waiting without progress, completed by the clue's own word 'time'.

clue.text: Canine companion

parts.note: canine here is the pointed tooth, and its companion in the mouth is a grinding back tooth

explanation.surface: A dog as a faithful friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine companion' suggests a pet dog, but the canine is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad back tooth used for grinding, sharing the jaw with the pointed eye tooth.

clue.text: VIPs finance authors?

definitions.meaning: members of the royal family, very important persons
payments to writers from each copy sold

explanation.surface: Important people paying for writers.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural can mean royal persons, and also the sums a writer earns per copy sold.

clue.text: Assassin's admission in Scottish isle

definitions.meaning: a killer confessing would say 'I kill', put as two words
an island of the Inner Hebrides famous for whisky

explanation.surface: A killer confesses on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the island's name as two words, a killer's confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer confessing says he kills, in two words; the same letters name a Hebridean whisky island.

clue.text: French general supplies drink…, including cooked meal

indicators.note: including means the drink holds the rearranged meal inside it

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of meal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French general supplies drinks with a cooked meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Gamelin commanded the French army in 1940; 'supplies' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Gamelin was the French commander-in-chief at the start of the Second World War.

clue.text: A new £1,000 piano, with key, is quite enough

indicators.note: new tells us the following letters are to be made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: L is the pound sign (from Latin libra) and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone buys a new grand piano complete with key, and finds it more than adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep A as it is, then 'new' rearranges L (pound), M (thousand), P (piano) and E (a key) into MPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ample is plentiful, more than sufficient for the need.

clue.text: Palindromic Dravidian language

indicators.note: Palindromic tells the solver that the language's name reads the same in both directions, which is all the wordplay there is

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry describes a South Indian tongue whose name is a palindrome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dravidian languages are those of southern India; the one spoken in Kerala has a name that reads identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the official tongue of the Indian state of Kerala, belonging to the Dravidian family alongside Tamil and Telugu.

clue.text: Company vehicle ?

parts.note: the saying 'two's company' turns 'company' into a pair of people, so the clue describes a car built for exactly two

explanation.surface: A firm's car is up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company vehicle' suggests a firm's car, but read through the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' it is a car for a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or aircraft with room for just a pair of occupants.

clue.text: Faithful ally-nothing, unusual

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of ally plus the nothing are put in an odd order

parts.note: O, the zero figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A faithful friend turns out to be worth nothing, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and loyal are synonyms, both describing steady allegiance.

clue.text: Tutor goes on tour

definitions.meaning: a private teacher who prepares a student, especially for exams
a long-distance bus, the vehicle a touring party travels in

explanation.surface: A teacher sets off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A private tutor is a sports-style trainer for exams, and the same word is the touring bus in British English.

clue.text: Wins so easily with cards on the table

definitions.meaning: winning without effort, the idiom used of an easy victory
a card player's holding laid face down on the table

explanation.surface: A card player wins comfortably with everything shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for winning effortlessly, and a literal description of cards laid face down on a table.

clue.text: Mind replacement entering club game?

indicators.note: entering means the rearranged letters go inside the club

parts.note: a baton is a short stick or truncheon, a club

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of mind are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A substitute brain is fitted at a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like the sports club of the surface, but it is a stick, the truncheon kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: A Poujadist, for instance, is so puffed up

parts.note: the word Poujadist finishes with the letters D, I, S, T, so it is a word with that ending

explanation.surface: A follower of the French populist Poujade is described as arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: Poujadists followed Pierre Poujade, a 1950s French populist. The clue's 'for instance, is so' asks you to see the word as one whose ending is DIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Distended means swollen or inflated by pressure from within.

clue.text: River birds seen on ships astern

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff
rails are marsh birds such as the water rail

explanation.surface: Birds of a river are seen perched at the back of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is a Welsh river through Cardiff; rails are wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffrails are the rails round the stern of a ship.

clue.text: Inexperience, shows up on the. Centre Court

definitions.meaning: rawness, the state of a novice

definitions.text: shows up on the. Centre Court
definitions.meaning: the grass colour seen on the main court at Wimbledon

explanation.surface: A novice player is exposed on Wimbledon's main court.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is the main grass tennis court at Wimbledon, so what shows up there is the colour of its turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raw or new to something is the first sense; the colour of grass on the Wimbledon court is the second.

clue.text: Losing 1,000 dollars he'd go easy

parts.note: G, short for grand, is slang for a thousand dollars
one who ambles goes at an easy pace

explanation.surface: After losing a thousand dollars, a man decides to take things easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a punter who loses a grand might well ease off.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter who has lost heavily on bets may be the kind of person who then takes care.

clue.text: Urgent message about sporting body supplying seats

indicators.note: about means the message goes around the sporting body

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, an urgent message
the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football

explanation.surface: An emergency call about a sports organisation concerns its seating.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is England's Football Association, the body that runs the national game.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofas are upholstered seats for several people.

clue.text: Could be one star in Roman politics

definitions.text: Could be one star in Roman politics

indicators.note: Could be signals that the letters of one star might become another word

explanation.surface: Someone could be a star of Roman political life.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a leading member of the Roman senate could be a political star.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the governing council of ancient Rome, a leading figure in its politics.

clue.text: Girl returned with Weller about four

indicators.note: returned says the whole built-up word is read from back to front
about means the Roman four goes inside Weller's name

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A girl came back with someone called Weller at around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller is the Cockney servant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; 'returned' turns the whole build-up, SIVAM, round.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, here standing for any girl.

clue.text: Some believe no magic remedy for poison

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people believe no magical cure exists for poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'remedy for poison' as the definition, but a remedy is not venom; the definition is 'poison' alone, and the page prints 'no magic' with no apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the poison injected by snakes, spiders and similar creatures.

clue.text: Hard thing to find in a laundry?.

definitions.text: Hard thing to find in a laundry?

parts.words: Hard thing to find in a laundry?
parts.note: a laundry holds bed linen and a pressing appliance, and together those two words name a rigid metal material

explanation.surface: Something difficult to locate in a laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard thing to find' reads as something elusive, but 'hard' describes the material, and the two words come from laundry items.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat rolled metal plate is hard, and its name joins two things found in a laundry: bed linen and a pressing appliance.

clue.text: Meaning one is 24?

definitions.meaning: the import or significance of something
the answer to 24 down is one of the five faculties of perception

explanation.surface: Asking what it means that one is twenty-four.
explanation.definitionFit: Significance is one sense; the other is a faculty such as sight, hearing or the one at 24.

clue.text: " Drink deep, or not the Pierian spring " (Pope)

definitions.text: " Drink deep, or not the Pierian spring " (Pope)

parts.words: Drink deep, or not the Pierian spring
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Pope's line warns that a little learning is dangerous, and the missing verb means to sample with the tongue

explanation.surface: A quotation from Pope's Essay on Criticism with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Alexander Pope's Essay on Criticism: 'A little learning is a dangerous thing; Drink deep, or ___ not the Pierian spring'. The Pierian spring was sacred to the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to sample a little, completing Pope's famous couplet.

clue.text: Sleep where they agreed?

definitions.meaning: a place where everyone bows their head in assent

explanation.surface: Asking where people went to sleep once they had agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical land east of Eden where Cain went is also the playful name for sleep, since nodding off is falling asleep; nodding is also how people show agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical place name became a jocular term for slumber, and nodding is a sign of agreement.

clue.text: Garment may be lost when punting

definitions.text: Garment may be lost when punting

parts.words: Garment may be lost when punting
parts.note: punting is British slang for betting, and to lose this top garment is the idiom for losing everything on a wager

explanation.surface: Clothing might be lost overboard while boating on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Punting suggests poling a flat boat on the river; in British slang it also means betting, and 'to lose your ___' is losing all you have.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttoned top garment, and losing it is the idiom for losing all one's money gambling.

clue.text: Tale 'by Cameron, needs revision:

indicators.note: needs revision says the letters of the name must be revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A story by a writer called Cameron needs editing.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story, especially of love or adventure.

clue.text: Hospital helper — might be Welsh?

definitions.meaning: an assistant who applies bandages and dressings for a surgeon
a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates, of the type named after Wales

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hospital assistant could be from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh ___ is a traditional sideboard with plate racks; the other sense is a surgeon's assistant who dresses wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's assistant who applies dressings, and a piece of kitchen furniture of the Welsh type.
